Advice on a Result

Source: R/advice.R
advice.Rd

Results of predictmeans functions carry short advice when this fit and these data call for a choice or a caution the user may not know about: an unbalanced design, empty cells, a covariate aliased with a factor, a singular fit, an extrapolated mean, few degrees of freedom, many tests, too few permutations, and so on. Advice is printed at the end of the result as an "Advice:" block (! a caution: the result may mislead as it stands; i a note: a choice worth knowing). It is never generic, and no test is run that was not asked for. advice() returns it as a data frame, for code and AI assistants.

options(predictmeans.advice = FALSE) stops the printing; the advice is still stored.

Usage

advice(x)

Arguments

x

A result of predictmeans(), contrastmeans(), anova() of an lmer or semireg fit, pm_check(), permmodels(), bootmodels(), R2_model(), residvariogram(), heritability(), varcomp(), se_ranef(), semireg(), semipred(), covariatemeans() or pm_slopes().

Value

A data frame with columns id (stable, listed below), level ("caution" or "note") and text; zero rows when there is no advice.

Advice ids

idfromwhen
nonestimable_meanspredictmeans, covariatemeanssome means cannot be estimated (NA)
empty_cellspredictmeansmeans average over the observed cells only
aliased_covariatepredictmeansa covariate is constant within a factor's levels
large_sepredictmeansa mean's SE is over 3 times the median SE
lsd_variespredictmeansthe average LSD judges some pair differently from its own test
bias_adjustpredictmeans, covariatemeansback-transformed means are a typical cluster's or a median, not the mean
contrast_common_cellscontrastmeanscontrasts are estimated on the cells their means share
small_dfpredictmeans, contrastmeansdegrees of freedom below 5
many_tests_unadjustedpredictmeans, contrastmeans6 or more requested tests with adj = "none"
singular_fitpredictmeans, contrastmeans, R2_model, semirega variance at zero or a correlation at +-1
anova_unbalanced_typeI, _typeII, _typeIIIanovaunbalanced data: what the type tests
anova_nested_in_dataanovaa factor nested in another in the data, without the nesting in the model
h2_standard_unbalancedheritabilitythe standard form with unequal plots per genotype or incomplete blocks
h2_forms_differheritabilitythe forms differ by more than 0.1
h2_above_oneheritabilitya family heritability above 1 (beyond or within its sampling error)
h2_genotype_zeroheritabilitythe genotypic variance estimated as 0
h2_genotype_nestedheritabilitygenotypes nested in a fixed factor
anova_empty_cellsanovaempty cells: no type tests a main effect over all cells
anova_covariate_zeroanovaType III with a covariate in an interaction (tests at covariate = 0)
check_<name>pm_checka check worth a look (the note of its row)
variogram_spatialresidvariogramneighbouring plots more alike than the model allows
variogram_neighboursresidvariogramneighbouring plots less alike than the model allows (competition)
variogram_trendresidvariogramthe variogram leaves the envelope at longer lags only
variogram_incompleteresidvariogrammore than 10% of the grid positions empty
ordinal_latent_averagepredictmeansclass probabilities at latent means averaged over other variables
ordinal_mean_classpredictmeansthe mean class scores the classes as equally spaced
ordinal_typical_subjectpredictmeansclmm class probabilities for a typical subject (random effects at 0)
class_separationpredictmeansa class with no observations at some levels (probability at 0, SEs not usable)
class_prob_averagepredictmeansclass probabilities averaged over other variables on the probability scale
class_prob_near_boundpredictmeansdifferences of probabilities near 0 or 1 (mean_type = "prob_diff")
class_referencepredictmeansmultinomial linear predictors depend on the reference class
class_crossingpredictmeanscumulative curves of a non-parallel fit cross: the means that use those points are NA
class_mean_outsidepredictmeanslimits of a mean class outside 1 to J (Wald limits on the class scale)

variance_test_boundaryvarcomphow to test a variance against zero (test = TRUE)

Examples

oats <- nlme::Oats
oats$nitro <- factor(oats$nitro)
fm <- lme4::lmer(log(yield) ~ nitro * Variety + (1 | Block), data = oats)
res <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro:Variety", pairwise = TRUE)
#> The response is log(yield): the means are also given back-transformed to the original scale (trans = I for the model scale only).
advice(res)
#>                      id level
#> 1           bias_adjust  note
#> 2 many_tests_unadjusted  note
#>                                                                                                                                                                                             text
#> 1 'response' is the median of the original scale (the geometric mean for a log), not the mean. If the mean on the original scale is wanted (totals, averages to report), use bias_adjust = TRUE.
#> 2                                      66 pairs tested without adjustment: some will be significant by chance. If they are a family, use adj = "holm" (any design) or "tukey"/"mvt" (all pairs).
